chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
If people knew how the creation began, no two would disagree.

Indeed God — Mighty and Majestic — before He created creation, said: 'Be sweet water! I shall create from you My Paradise and the people of My obedience. And be bitter water! I shall create from you My Fire and the people of My disobedience.'
Then He commanded them both, so they were blended. Thus it came about that the believer begets the disbeliever and the disbeliever begets the believer.

Then He took clay from the surface of the earth and kneaded it with an intense kneading, and they were like tiny particles crawling about. So He said to the companions of the right hand: 'To Paradise in peace!' And He said to the companions of the left hand: 'To the Fire, and I do not care!'

Then He commanded a fire, so it blazed. He said to the companions of the left: 'Enter it!' But they were terrified of it. So He said to the companions of the right: 'Enter it!' And they entered it. So He said: 'Be cool and a safety!' And it became cool and a safety.

The companions of the left said: 'O Lord, forgive us!' He said: 'I have forgiven you, so enter it.' They went but were terrified of it. Thus from that point, obedience and disobedience were established — these ones do not have the capacity to be from those, nor those from these.

key_terms.أصحاب الشمال: Companions of the left hand — those destined for Fire, a Quranic expression (56:9)
key_terms.أصحاب اليمين: Companions of the right hand — those destined for Paradise, a Quranic expression (56:8)
key_terms.ابتداء الخلق: The origination/beginning of creation — the cosmological event before the physical world
key_terms.الطاعة والمعصية: Obedience and disobedience — the fundamental moral division established at creation

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam al-Baqir say about how creation began and why believers beget disbelievers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrates a cosmological hadith explaining the primordial origins of belief and disbelief. Before creation, God designated two primordial waters — one sweet for Paradise and the obedient, one bitter for Hell and the disobedient — and then mixed them, which is why a believer can beget a disbeliever and vice versa. The hadith then describes the covenant event (mithaq) where the pre-existent souls were tested with fire: those of the right hand entered obediently and were made safe, while those of the left refused even after being forgiven, establishing the eternal division between the obedient and the disobedient.
word_analysis: but they were terrified of it
